questions.q: What is the name of the line segment that connects two points on a circle and passes through the center?
questions.a: The line segment is called the diameter. A student who answers "radius" confuses the line from the center to the edge with the line stretching across the entire circle.

questions.q: If a circle has a radius of 5 cm, why is it incorrect to say the diameter is 5 cm as well?
questions.a: It is incorrect because the diameter must stretch from one side to the other, covering two radii; thus, it is 10 cm. A student who says it remains 5 cm fails to understand that the diameter represents the full width, not just the distance from the center.

questions.q: A circular park has a diameter of 20 meters. If a path is built from the center to the edge, how long will the path be?
questions.a: The path (radius) will be 10 meters. We find this by dividing the diameter (20m) by 2 (20 ÷ 2 = 10). A student who answers 40m has mistakenly multiplied instead of dividing.

questions.q: Why is the diameter considered a special type of chord?
questions.a: The diameter is a chord because it connects two points on the circle, but it is special because it is the longest possible chord as it passes through the center. A student who cannot explain this does not see the relationship between a general chord and the diameter.

questions.q: If you draw a chord that does not pass through the center, is it still a diameter? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is not a diameter. A diameter must pass through the center to be the longest line segment; any other chord is shorter. A student who says "yes" does not understand the unique requirement of the diameter passing through the center.

questions.q: Draw a circle and mark a point A on the edge and point B on the edge. Draw a chord AB and an arc AB. How do they differ?
questions.a: The chord AB is a straight line segment, while the arc AB is the curved path along the edge of the circle. A poor answer would fail to distinguish between the straight distance and the curved boundary.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A circle is a closed plane figure where every point on the edge is at an equal distance from a fixed center point; the line segments ______ this shape include the radius (center to edge), diameter (edge to edge through center), and chord (any two points on the edge).
Fill in the blank: Have you ever looked at a bicycle wheel or a round dinner plate and wondered how we ______ its parts?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to draw, label, and distinguish between a radius, diameter, chord, and arc on a given circle and calculate the diameter when the radius is provided.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Have you ever looked at a bicycle wheel or a round dinner plate and ______ how we describe its parts?
